content_html_sanitized:
HHS Rules That California Patients Have A Right To Adequate Pain Medication
– Context For Medical Marijuana

(Marijuananews note: The obvious question is – if patients have the right to effective pain medication, and only cannabis provides adequate relief, then why would they not have a right to use cannabis? Or is there also a "marijuana exception" to patients’ rights?)

July 14, 1999
From The Houston Chronicle
viewpoints@chron.com
http://www.chron.com/
http://www.chron.com/content/hcitalk/index.html

RIGHT TO PAIN MEDICATION

WASHINGTON—A ruling by the Department of Health and Human Services will force doctors and other health care workers in California to tell patients they have the right to pain medication, activists said on Tuesday.

See
NORML Special Bulletin -- IOM Acknowledges:
"There is no clear alternative for people suffering from chronic conditions
that might be relieved by smoking marijuana, such as pain or AIDS wasting."
But Still Opposes Smoked Marijuana --
and
Three Articles On Pain -- From Washington, The UK, And Arkansas –
And Two Are Even About Medical Marijuana -- Analysis By Richard Cowan
and
Aspirin And Related Drugs Are 15th Leading Cause Of Death In DEAland
Context For Medical Marijuana
and links

They said they hoped the ruling would not only eventually make pain relief more available to all Americans, but might also give desperate patients an alternative to suicide.

The ruling came from the federal Health Care Financing Administration, which oversees Medicare and Medicaid.
